newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-THE FRENCH KEEP IT IN THE FAMILY.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-THE FRENCH KEEP IT IN THE FAMILY.

text.p: French hopes in the opening race of the Alpine skiing world championships on Monday rest with two cousins, one with a beard and one without, who live a sprint down the road from each other.
The bearded one with the big smile is Luc Alphand, current super-G, downhill and overall World Cup leader.
His cousin, the pensive fresh-faced one, is 22-year-old Benjamin Melquiond, whose parents' house is about 100 metres from Alphand's in Serre-Chavalier .
With Adrien Duvillard out of the running after a serious crash at Wengen, Alphand and Melquiond are the only French racers in the super-G.
The two men, separated by 10 years of experience but otherwise sitting alongside each other, appeared at a news conference on Sunday ahead of the opening race.
Alphand, winner of three World Cup downhills and the most recent super-G this season, fielded the questions.
He said his recent super-G win in Laax was a "psychological plus" that could give him a boost.

The Sestriere Kandahar-Banchetta piste was better than those of the last two world championships and it seemed to him the same as the one he remembered from 1983 when he won the world junior title in the Italian resort.
Melquiond sat somewhat awkwardly and smiled. With little previous experience, he had little to add.
"This is my first championships but I have ambitions as well," he said later. "I'm not just here to come 10th."
For a man in his debut World Cup season, those may sound like brave words but Melquiond is not joking.
His side of the family has skiing in the blood and his father Jules was a contemporary of the legendary Jean-Claude Killy. Benjamin was also 1994 junior super-G world champion.
"It's good to race with him," he said of Alphand, whose mother is Melquiond's father's cousin.
"I think we're cousins once removed," he explained.
"I profit from his experience and his good humour because he is a fun person to be around."
"But the help stops at the starting gate. He gives you the information when he gets to the bottom of the piste but after that, well it's up to you to do what you have to do.
"We're cousins, we're friends but we don't share everything."
Alphand, who is a favourite here to take the first gold medal of an often injury-disrupted career, was inevitably a big influence on Melquiond's early career.
"Even if he wasn't getting the results he is getting now, he was still always an example to us," he said.
"I have always followed everything he has done."
Michel Vion, head coach of the French team, sees some stylistic similarities between the two as well.
"They are two skiers with pretty similar styles, very gentle on the snow. Luc has more experience, has put more work in and is even lighter. But Benjamin is very light."
"They are both very calm and patient. They were both world junior champions so there is already a resemblance.
"Benjamin has a serious future. He's a good hope. He needs to be because when Luc stops, we need a replacement.
"He is the future."
